sections.passage: A circuit is set up to study the relationship between the potential difference across a resistor and the current through it. A cell, a key, an ammeter, a rheostat and the resistor are connected one after another in a loop, and a voltmeter is connected across the resistor. As the rheostat is adjusted, the voltmeter and ammeter readings increase in the same proportion, and the graph of V against I is a straight line. Fuses and miniature circuit breakers (MCBs) are added to household circuits for safety. (April 2024)

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Find the currents flowing in 2 Ω, 4 Ω and 6 Ω resistors connected in parallel across a 24 V battery.
questions.answer: In parallel each resistor has 24 V across it. I = V/R: 2 Ω — 12 A; 4 Ω — 6 A; 6 Ω — 4 A (total 22 A).

questions.q: State Ohm's law. Define the unit of resistance.
questions.answer: The current through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across its ends, provided its temperature and other physical conditions remain the same (V = IR). One ohm is the resistance of a conductor through which 1 A flows when a potential difference of 1 V is applied across it.

questions.q: How many electrons make one coulomb of charge?
questions.answer: Charge on one electron = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. Number of electrons = 1/(1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹) = 6.25 × 10¹⁸.

questions.q: State two advantages of connecting household appliances in parallel rather than in series.
questions.answer: (1) Each appliance gets the full mains voltage and draws the current it needs. (2) Each can be switched on or off independently, and if one fails the others keep working; the total resistance is also lower.

questions.q: Calculate the work done in moving a charge of 3 C across two points having a potential difference of 24 V.
How many units of electricity will a 60 W lamp use in 30 days if it is lit for 4 hours daily?
questions.answer: Energy = P × t = 60 W × 4 h × 30 = 7200 Wh = 7.2 kWh, i.e. 7.2 units.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: State Joule's law of heating. A 5 Ω resistor is connected to a 10 V battery for 2 minutes. Calculate the heat produced in joules.
questions.answer: The heat produced in a conductor is directly proportional to the square of the current, the resistance and the time for which current flows: H = I²Rt. I = V/R = 10/5 = 2 A; t = 120 s. H = 2² × 5 × 120 = 2400 J.

questions.q: (a) An electric iron is marked 220 V–50 Hz and 1 kW. Explain these markings. Can it be used on both AC and DC? (b) Calculate the resistance of its heating element.
questions.answer: (a) 220 V is the voltage at which it is designed to work; 50 Hz is the frequency of the AC mains; 1 kW is the power it uses at 220 V. Yes, it works on DC too, because the heating effect (I²R) does not depend on the direction of the current. (b) R = V²/P = 220²/1000 = 48.4 Ω.

questions.q: Derive the expression for the equivalent resistance of three resistors in series. What is the total resistance of 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 6 Ω in series?
questions.answer: In series the same current I flows through each, and V = V1 + V2 + V3 = IR1 + IR2 + IR3. If Rs is the equivalent resistance, V = IRs, so Rs = R1 + R2 + R3. For 2, 3 and 6 Ω: Rs = 11 Ω.

questions.q: An electric iron of resistance 25 Ω takes a current of 5 A. Calculate the heat developed in 1 minute.
How much time will a 2 kW immersion rod take to raise the temperature of 1 litre of water from 30 °C to 60 °C? (Specific heat of water = 4.18 × 10³ J kg⁻¹ °C⁻¹)
questions.answer: Heat needed = mcθ = 1 × 4180 × 30 = 125 400 J. Heat supplied = Pt = 2000 × t. So t = 125 400/2000 = 62.7 s.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: (a) Derive the relation for the equivalent resistance of three resistors connected in parallel. (b) Resistors of 10 Ω, 15 Ω and 30 Ω are connected in parallel to a 12 V battery. Calculate (i) the total resistance of the circuit and (ii) the current through the 10 Ω resistor.
questions.answer: (a) In parallel each resistor has the same potential difference V, and the total current is the sum of the branch currents: I = I1 + I2 + I3 = V/R1 + V/R2 + V/R3. If Rp is the equivalent resistance, I = V/Rp, so 1/Rp = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + 1/R3. (b) (i) 1/Rp = 1/10 + 1/15 + 1/30 = (3 + 2 + 1)/30 = 6/30, so Rp = 5 Ω. (ii) The 10 Ω resistor has 12 V across it: I = 12/10 = 1.2 A.

questions.q: (a) Derive an expression for the heat produced in a conductor when current flows through it. (b) What is electric power? Derive its expression in terms of I and R. (c) A torch bulb is marked 3.0 V, 500 mA. Calculate its power and resistance.
questions.answer: (a) Moving charge Q through a potential difference V needs work W = VQ = VIt (Q = It). By Ohm's law V = IR, so W = I²Rt, which appears as heat: H = I²Rt. (b) Electric power is the rate of using electrical energy: P = W/t = VI = (IR)I = I²R (also V²/R); unit watt. (c) P = VI = 3.0 × 0.5 = 1.5 W; R = V/I = 3.0/0.5 = 6 Ω.
